title: DS Lodge in two and a half minutes
voice_note: Irish English (Dublin). Warm, brisk, conversational. Smile on the opening and the closing. Do not read like a robot: short breaths between lines, stress the numbers.

lines: Two houses. Dozens of beds. One clear picture.
This is how 47/48 Amiens and Connolly can run on live information.
Right now, the story of a night lives in notebooks, calls and memory.
So by the time it reaches the office, it is already old news.
What if everyone worked from the same page, as it happens?
Here is the Admin's Home. Both houses, live.
Who's in, which beds are free, who's on duty, and what's waiting on you.
Pick a period, and every number moves with it.
In the house, it starts with the bed map.
Admit someone with their PASS ID, and the system spots former residents straight away.
Cancel a bed, and it's free for the next person.
At each check, one tap per resident: seen, not seen, or absent.
Launch it, and the Admin knows the count before the kettle's boiled.
Anything worth knowing goes in the Handover, once.
Tag it, mention a colleague, and urgent ones land on the manager's phone.
Nothing deleted. Every correction is kept.
A leak? A repair request with a deadline and a priority.
The Tesco order is matched to the delivery the house receives, and the note writes itself.
Every tap in the houses feeds one live picture.
No double typing. No chasing. Just the facts, as they happen.
And that is what makes better decisions possible.
Reports by period and by house.
Occupancy, warnings, maintenance, no-shows, spending.
Click any number, and you see the records behind it.
And if anyone asks who did what, and when?
The Audit trail has the answer, with the before and the after.
It works on a phone too, and if the internet drops, there's an offline sheet you can print.
Know sooner. Decide better.
DS Lodge. Sorted.
